A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ANN-SNN conversion work despite the changed title and presentation. The complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original classification, segmentation, and detection experiments, conversion ablations, and energy estimates.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments on those tasks, plus video classification, delayed-evaluation analyses, and measured conversion times.

M1.justification: The core threshold-balancing, channel-wise threshold, and pre-neuron max-pooling procedures remain. v2 adds data-dependent delay selection using an estimated first-spike time and t0 = min(estimated delay, T - 4), extending v1's fixed-window evaluation. The written threshold update also drops the 1/N normalization. These are localized procedural revisions.

E1.justification: v2 retains ImageNet, Pascal VOC/SBD, and COCO coverage and adds video classification on a Kinetics-400 subset using MC3-18 and R3D-18 (Section 5.6, Table 3). This extends evaluation from still images to spatiotemporal inputs and action recognition.

E2.justification: v2 adds QCFS to the integration comparison and includes QCFS and ACP in the main ImageNet comparison; ACP previously appeared only in the integration experiment. The LCP/ACP integration comparisons remain. v1's Figure 1 comparison with direct and hybrid training methods is removed, substantially changing the comparison scope.

E3.justification: Appendix D changes VOC calibration from 5/6 to 4/5 dataset traversals for FCN/DeepLab and detection calibration from 1000 to 5000 iterations. Reported ImageNet and detection preprocessing also changes. New protocols include the 12000/7881-video calibration/test split, video-level clip aggregation, and conversion-time comparisons using the same 4090 GPU environment.

E4.justification: v2 adds an explicit delayed-evaluation ablation, a delay-length sensitivity study across four inference budgets, QCFS integration analysis, and conversion-time scaling analysis. v1's clipping-error convergence plot is removed. The iteration-count sensitivity study and appendix detection/segmentation example grids are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the empirical results. v2 continues reporting point estimates.

E6.justification: Numerous scores change: ImageNet ResNet-34 accuracy at 32 steps changes from 59.03% to 64.88%, while ResNet-18 at 512 steps changes from 69.66% to 69.21%. These accompany method/protocol revisions, so they are not same-setting gains or losses. v2 adds QCFS, video, and timing results and removes the 512-step segmentation/detection columns. Existing LCP/ACP integration scores and energy estimates remain.

T1.justification: The conversion-error bound, max-pooling theorem, and their proofs remain substantively intact. v2 adds the delayed-window relation and first-spike-time estimate in Equations 18–19, corrects the preceding-layer threshold index in Equation 2, and revises the update-rule normalization and summation in Appendix B.

C1.justification: The central claim of inexpensive, high-performance conversion of pretrained ANNs remains. v2 reframes it around inference-scale complexity, makes delay selection an explicit contribution, extends claimed applicability to video, and proposes online on-chip conversion. These refine and extend the existing thesis rather than replace it.

C2.justification: v2 explains how spike propagation delays motivate the evaluation window and why one-time threshold optimization differs from timestep-specific calibration. Appendix G acknowledges LCP's timing advantage at 32 steps. The integration claim is qualified from improvement at all timesteps to most timesteps; the broad performance/cost and architectural limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 adds a code-availability URL, delay-estimation and inference pseudocode, explicit ResNet architecture distinctions, and timing hardware information. Video implementation details include 15 fps, five 16-frame clips per video, and 112×112 crops. These substantially expand the documented information needed to reproduce and interpret the experiments.

R1.justification: v2 expands citations to recent calibration, conversion, and spiking-transformer work, including FTBC and unified optimization, and adds video-related references. It explicitly positions delay selection as building on Hwang et al.'s delayed evaluation. The underlying distinction between backpropagation-dependent learning and lightweight conversion remains.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, related work, and methodological explanations receive extensive editing, with revised terminology and notation. Experiments are reorganized to lead with integration and separate ablation, iteration, and delay analyses. The appendices are presented as supplementary material and gain a training-cost discussion.

P2.justification: The document changes from single-column to two-column layout. Figures 1–2 are redesigned, Figure 3 is recomposed, and a delay-sensitivity figure and timing table are added. Comparison tables are restructured. The existing appendix example grids are relocated and relabeled as Figures S1–S2, with their image content unchanged.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens support for the central efficiency claim through measured same-hardware conversion times in Appendix G, replacing reliance on largely qualitative or estimated cost comparisons. Dedicated delay-selection tests, broader validation, and improved implementation documentation also strengthen the paper. These gains outweigh the removed convergence analysis, although changed protocols prevent interpreting revised headline scores as controlled performance improvements.
